what: People with specific needs only require a fraction of features in bloated SaaS and prefer to vibe-code personal tools that own their data rather than lock into vendors. Recurring anti-cloud, offline-first, privacy-focused demand (~7% of 'wish there was an app' requests).
why_us: High engagement signal of subscription fatigue and preference for simple, local, personal software over multi-feature cloud platforms. Strong willingness-to-pay in adjacent niches like finance/education.
revenue: N/A (demand signal); potential $10-50/mo personal tools or open-source + premium

what: Analysis of 9300+ 'I wish there was an app for this' posts shows anti-cloud/privacy/offline-first as significant trend, productivity highest volume but finance highest pay intent, education/self-improvement high willingness to pay.
why_us: Aggregated real demand data with specific niches having 'I will pay' language; long angry posts are free product specs.

what: Solo founder building AgentaOS with 0 employees and 10 AI hires reached $10k MRR.
why_us: Concrete recent example of AI-augmented solo SaaS hitting meaningful revenue; shows barrier to entry is low ($200 Claude plan mentioned elsewhere).

what: Widespread complaints about SaaS pricing: too expensive (Pocket FM ~$400/book, DoFasting $80/3mo), coin systems on top of subscriptions (Liftapp.ai), subscription fatigue (Splice), hidden fees/trickery (MuseScore, Rocket Money bill negotiation), price hikes forcing switches (PRTG to Zabbix).
why_us: Recurring pain of overpricing, poor transparency, and value mismatch in paid tools; opportunity for cheaper, transparent, narrower alternatives.
revenue: N/A; users explicitly calling out waste of money and seeking cheaper options

what: Barrier to entry for challenging established SaaS is now ~$200/mo Claude Max plan; cracked founder can build MVP-level competitor in months.
why_us: Signals rapid AI-enabled micro-SaaS creation; revenue potential in niches with existing paid demand but poor UX/pricing.
revenue: Potential $1k-$10k MRR range for successful wrappers (median indie ~$145-500)
